_comment: A one-time external cross-check, dated and recorded rather than re-run. The witnesses (PROJ, GEOTRANS, GeographicLib) are Python packages that are NOT dependencies of this repository — running them again needs a virtualenv, so their results are frozen here. What survives and is re-asserted on every build is records/reference-points.json and records/reference-pairs.json, which are the residue of this comparison. check.mjs re-proves those on every build with no dependencies at all.
sample: 4,000 pseudo-random points from a fixed seed spanning 80°S–84°N and all 60 UTM zones; 1,500 random point pairs for distance and bearing.

measurements.label: UTM vs PROJ 9.5.1
measurements.note: Worst disagreement in forward easting or northing of any single one of the 4,000 points, in metres. The inverse transform agrees to the same order.

measurements.label: MGRS vs NGA GEOTRANS
measurements.note: Every 5-digit MGRS string produced here is character-for-character identical to the one GEOTRANS produces for the same point.

measurements.label: Distance vs GeographicLib
measurements.note: Over 1,500 random pairs. Initial and final bearings agree to within 1 × 10⁻⁵ arcseconds.

measurements.label: Reproduce it
measurements.note: No dependencies and no network. It reads src/coord.mjs and asserts it against the frozen records below, so the arithmetic and the published tables cannot drift apart.

witnesses.name: NGA GEOTRANS
witnesses.version: as bundled by the Python `mgrs` package

known_limits: Vincenty's method does not converge for very nearly antipodal pairs. The converter refuses those rather than printing a wrong distance; GeographicLib would solve them and is not shipped here.
The cross-check covers 80°S–84°N. UTM and MGRS are undefined outside that band and the converter says so instead of extrapolating.
The comparison was run once, on one machine, in Node 25. It has not been run in a browser engine.
